title: Typesense crashes when locale of the field is ja (Japanese) in Ubuntu 22.04 ARM64 Docker
body:
## Description

Typesense crashes if client tries to import Japanese in `locale: "ja"` field.

## Steps to reproduce

1. Create a collection that contains `locale: "ja"` field. I used the code using Node.js with `typesense@1.5.3`:

```ts
await typesense.collections().create({ name: "test", fields: [{ name: "japanese", type: "string", locale: "ja" }] });
```

2. Then, import the document to the collection created.

```ts
await typesense
      .collections("test")
      .documents()
      .import([{ japanese: "こんにちは" }, { japanese: "またね" }], { action: "upsert" });
```

## Expected Behavior

Typesense should not crash when importing documents in Japanese.

comments.body:
Hello, @participant1! I apologize for the delayed response as I was conducting further investigation into the issue. Upon thorough examination, I discovered the cause of the problem by comparing the code I provided as an example with your own code.

It appears that there were no errors in either of the codes. However, upon further analysis using my original document, I identified the specific factor that is leading to the issue.

When you set the field `locale` as `ja` (Japanese) and have duplicate values at the same time, it triggers an error that is unique to this locale. This error does not occur with other locales. To reproduce this, consider the following code snippet that demonstrates how Typesense crashes and becomes unreachable:

```ts
result = await typesense
  .collections("test")
  .documents()
  .import([
    { japanese: "こんにちは" },
    { japanese: "こんにちは" },
    { japanese: "またね" }
  ], { action: "upsert" });
```

Thank you for investigating the issue. If you require any resources from me, please don't hesitate to reach out to me.

comments.author: participant2
comments.body:
When we index Japanese, we convert all Kanji characters to Hiragana. The library that we use to do that is choking on the following:

"魈"

We've to figure out why that's happening and fix that.

comments.author: reporter
comments.body: @participant2, After further investigation, I discovered that the order of `query_by` is the issue. When I placed `name_kr` first in the `query_by` field, the Japanese search was unavailable. I attempted to fix this by placing `name_jp` first, but doing so resulted in inaccurate Korean search results.

comments.author: participant2
comments.body: The query string is tokenized based on the locale of the first `query_by` field. We probably need to think about how to tokenize the query separately for each locale independently when multiple languages are used.
